title: M74 — The Phantom Galaxy
subtitle: Spiral galaxy in Pisces, 30 million light-years away
facts: M74 is a grand-design spiral galaxy seen almost face-on. Spitzer's infrared eye sees the dust that glows between the stars, which is why the arms read as ribbons rather than as points of light.
journeyIntro: Let's start with a galaxy. Put your finger on the picture, or use the arrow keys. The middle is bright. The edges are nearly empty. Listen for the difference.

hotspots.name: The galactic core
hotspots.text: The centre, where the stars are packed so tightly that the whole middle glows white. Here the sound is high and full, because the picture is at its brightest.

hotspots.name: The upper arm
hotspots.text: A spiral arm, lit up in pink. This is an infrared picture, so what glows here is warm dust, not starlight — the galaxy's own smoke, heated from inside.

hotspots.name: The lower arm
hotspots.text: The other arm, thinner and cooler. Notice how the sound thins out as the dust fades — the pitch stays, but the brightness drains away.

hotspots.name: The dust factory
hotspots.text: A dark lane of cold dust. In infrared it is almost silent here, and that silence is information: this is where new stars are being built, hidden from ordinary light.
